newsitem.title: USA: NY Fed's McDonough says N.J. to continue recovery.
newsitem.headline: NY Fed's McDonough says N.J. to continue recovery.

text.p: Federal Reserve Bank of New York President William McDonough said New Jersey's job growth will accelerate modestly in 1997, despite the potential for moderately slower growth nationwide.

Economists at the New York Fed believe New Jersey's job growth will accelerate to 1.1 percent in 1997 from 0.9 percent in 1996, McDonough told the New Jersey Council on Economic Education on Wednesday evening.
"We expect close to 40,000 new jobs will be added next year in New Jersey," he said in his address.
McDonough attributed the acceleration in job growth to the strength in the region's key private sectors and a slowing in the recent rapid pace of decline in manufacturing and utilities.

"Business and consumer services are expected to be the driving forces for the private sector," McDonough said, adding "the restructurings will continue, but at a slower pace and with less of a drag on overall job growth."
McDonough said many challenges lie ahead for the state's cities and counties, including rapid technological changes and the shifting of budget responsibilities from the federal government to states.
"Technological advancements may reduce manufacturing employment in New Jersey," said McDonough, "but they also make it possible to attract financial services."
Job growth is only one measure of economic well-being, added McDonough. "Personal income also is growing at a reasonable clip in New Jersey -- about on par with that of the nation."
